persona.name: dumper
persona.reply: You over-explain. Answer what it asks from your knowledge bank, then add one or two sentences it did not ask for: a fact from the bank it has not asked about yet, or harmless backstory (who it is for, why, a worry). Never add a new requirement that is not in the bank. If it asks whether to proceed, say yes and add one more remark. Two to four sentences.
persona.giveUp: ok ok, just do whatever you think is best, honestly i trust you
persona.nudge: Oh, please just go ahead and try it anyway. I'd rather have something than nothing, and I know the free plan has its limits, that's fine by me.

bank.The request in full, as you would have w: Make a 10-second vertical promo for Northside Gym. Use a welcoming gym scene, not hardcore bodybuilding, with upbeat music and no voiceover. Keep these details on screen together for the last 5 seconds: “Northside Gym”, “18 Cedar Road”, “Mon–Fri 6am–10pm”, “Sat–Sun 8am–6pm”. Big enough to read on a phone.
bank.Business name and address: Northside Gym; 18 Cedar Road. Do not add a city, postcode or other contact details.
bank.Text timing: Show the name, address and both hours lines together throughout the last 5 seconds.
bank.Format and duration: Vertical 9:16, 10 seconds, readable on a phone.
bank.Visuals and style: A welcoming gym scene, not hardcore bodybuilding. Specific scene, colours and transitions are your call.
bank.Audio and language: Upbeat music, no voiceover. English text.

messages.text: Could you make a promo for Northside Gym with a welcoming gym scene rather than hardcore bodybuilding? I want people to feel comfortable about the idea of going to the gym, because I know it can feel a little intimidating at first. I’m probably overthinking how it will come across, but that’s why I’m explaining it all. It should have upbeat music and no voiceover, and what I’m after is a 10-second vertical video. For the last 5 seconds, please keep all these details on screen together: “Northside Gym”, “18 Cedar Road”, “Mon–Fri 6am–10pm”, “Sat–Sun 8am–6pm”. Make that text big enough to read on a phone.
